title: Commercial cells and fuel cells; Electrode potentials and the SHE; Cell potentials and feasibility
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Chemistry (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: RX06#t2 term and clue written for the game; RX06#t3 term and clue written for the game; RX06#t4 term and clue written for the game; RX04#t4 term and clue written for the game. Questions: RX04#N.4b, RX05#N.2b, RX06#N.6b, RX04#N.10b, RX05#N.4b, RX06#N.10, RX04#N.13, RX05#N.7, RX06#N.11, RX05#N.15.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Anion
items.clue: Negative particle such as NO₃⁻, moving into the zinc side as Zn²⁺ builds up.

items.label: Cation
items.clue: Positive particle such as K⁺, moving into the copper side as Cu²⁺ is used up.

items.label: Fuel cell
items.clue: Device fed continuously with H₂ and O₂; it never needs electrical recharging.

items.label: Potential difference
items.clue: What is measured between two half-cells; one half-cell alone can never give a reading.

questions.stem: In a galvanic cell built from a Zn electrode in Zn(NO₃)₂(aq) and a Cu electrode in Cu(NO₃)₂(aq), the zinc electrode loses mass and the copper electrode gains mass as the cell operates. Which half-reaction occurs at the anode?

options.text: Zn²⁺(aq) + 2 e⁻ → Zn(s)
Zn(s) → Zn²⁺(aq) + 2 e⁻
Cu(s) → Cu²⁺(aq) + 2 e⁻
Cu²⁺(aq) + 2 e⁻ → Cu(s)

questions.explanation: The zinc electrode loses mass because zinc atoms lose electrons and enter the solution as Zn²⁺ ions. This oxidation occurs at the anode.

questions.stem: The standard reduction potentials at 25°C are +0.80 V for Ag⁺(aq) + e⁻ → Ag(s) and −0.14 V for Sn²⁺(aq) + 2 e⁻ → Sn(s). What is E° for the reaction 2 Ag(s) + Sn²⁺(aq) → 2 Ag⁺(aq) + Sn(s)?
questions.explanation: As written, Sn²⁺ is reduced and Ag is oxidized, so E° = −0.14 V − (+0.80 V) = −0.94 V. The coefficient 2 does not change the Ag⁺/Ag potential; the negative sign shows the reaction as written is thermodynamically unfavored.

questions.stem: Which statement about the electrodes of galvanic and electrolytic cells is correct?

options.text: Oxidation occurs at the anode in galvanic cells and in electrolytic cells
Oxidation occurs at the anode in galvanic cells but at the cathode in electrolytic cells
The anode is the electrode that gains mass in both galvanic and electrolytic cells
The cathode is where cations are produced in galvanic cells and in electrolytic cells

questions.explanation: For all electrochemical cells, oxidation occurs at the anode and reduction at the cathode.

questions.stem: Standard reduction potentials at 25 °C: K⁺(aq) + e⁻ → K(s), E° = −2.92 V · Ni²⁺(aq) + 2 e⁻ → Ni(s), E° = −0.25 V · 2 H⁺(aq) + 2 e⁻ → H₂(g), E° = 0.00 V · Br₂(l) + 2 e⁻ → 2 Br⁻(aq), E° = +1.07 V. Which order lists the species from most easily reduced to least easily reduced?

options.text: K⁺ > Ni²⁺ > H⁺ > Br₂
K⁺ > Br₂ > Ni²⁺ > H⁺
Br₂ > H⁺ > K⁺ > Ni²⁺
Br₂ > H⁺ > Ni²⁺ > K⁺

questions.explanation: The more positive the E°, the more easily the left-hand species is reduced: +1.07, 0.00, −0.25, −2.92 V.

questions.stem: For the reaction Ni(s) + Zn²⁺(aq) → Ni²⁺(aq) + Zn(s), E°cell = −0.51 V at 25°C. Which statement about this reaction under standard conditions is correct?

options.text: It is thermodynamically favored, because a negative potential means energy is released
It is thermodynamically unfavored, so it proceeds only with an external potential
It is thermodynamically unfavored, so it occurs on its own but only very slowly
It is thermodynamically unfavored, so it cannot be made to occur under any conditions

questions.explanation: A negative cell potential means ΔG° is positive. The reaction proceeds only in an electrolytic cell, with an applied potential greater than 0.51 V.

questions.stem: Which statement about fuel cells, non-rechargeable cells and rechargeable cells is correct?

options.text: A fuel cell supplies electricity for as long as its fuel and oxygen are supplied.
A rechargeable cell stores electricity, which it releases unchanged when used.
A hydrogen fuel cell produces only water, so using one causes no pollution of any kind.
A fuel cell burns its fuel and converts the heat released to electrical energy.

questions.explanation: Its reactants are fed in continuously and products removed, so it doesn't run down like a cell with a fixed amount of reactants.

questions.stem: A standard Pb²⁺/Pb half-cell is connected to a standard hydrogen electrode. The voltmeter reads 0.13 V. Electrons flow through the wire from the lead electrode to the hydrogen electrode. Which statement is correct?

options.text: E°(Pb²⁺/Pb) = +0.13 V, because the voltmeter reading gives the lead electrode's potential directly, sign included.
E°(Pb²⁺/Pb) = −0.13 V, which is the absolute potential of the lead electrode on its own.
E°(Pb²⁺/Pb) = −0.13 V; the reading is the difference from the hydrogen electrode, which is 0 V by convention.
No reaction happens at the hydrogen electrode, because its E° is 0 V.

questions.stem: The standard reduction potentials at 25°C are +0.34 V for Cu²⁺(aq) + 2 e⁻ → Cu(s) and −0.74 V for Cr³⁺(aq) + 3 e⁻ → Cr(s). What is ΔG° for the reaction 2 Cr(s) + 3 Cu²⁺(aq) → 2 Cr³⁺(aq) + 3 Cu(s)? (F = 96,485 C/mol e⁻)

options.text: −208 kJ/mol_rxn
−521 kJ/mol_rxn
−625 kJ/mol_rxn
−232 kJ/mol_rxn

questions.stem: A car's lead–acid battery is recharged by the engine many times. During use, solid lead(II) sulfate forms on both electrodes: Pb(s) + SO₄²⁻(aq) → PbSO₄(s) + 2e⁻ PbO₂(s) + 4H⁺(aq) + SO₄²⁻(aq) + 2e⁻ → PbSO₄(s) + 2H₂O(l) Why can this battery be recharged?

options.text: Its sulfuric acid stores electricity, which the engine tops up.
The PbSO₄ stays on the electrodes, so a current can turn it back into Pb and PbO₂.
Charging runs the same two reactions again, only faster.
Lead atoms never lose electrons, so the cell is never used up.

questions.explanation: The products stay where they formed. An external current drives both half-equations backwards, re-forming the reactants.

questions.stem: A cell uses a chlorine half-cell: Cl₂(g) + 2e⁻ ⇌ 2Cl⁻(aq), E° = +1.36 V. Which metal half-cell, joined to it, gives the largest E°cell? Mg²⁺/Mg −2.37 V · Zn²⁺/Zn −0.76 V · Cu²⁺/Cu +0.34 V · Ag⁺/Ag +0.80 V

options.text: Silver, because +1.36 + 0.80 gives the largest total
Copper, because copper is a very good electrical conductor
Magnesium, because its very negative E° makes the largest gap
Zinc, because zinc is used in most everyday cells

questions.explanation: Mg gives up electrons most readily of the four. E°cell = +1.36 − (−2.37) = +3.73 V.
